name: pcb-a-power
title: PCB-A POWER + I/O

finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._stitch_prune_why: 12 September 2026, A24, and this is the board that presented the case the tool was written for. A's route laid /PA_SLOPE and /PA_RT across In2 within 0.5 mm of the locked VBAT stitch via at (101.5, 100.5), the fill retreated by its clearance, and the via's plane end ended 0.91 mm from the nearest VBAT copper: a via connected to a 0.2 mm escape stub at one end and to nothing at the other. `check_pcb_a` refused the board for it, ONE failure of 799 checks, on a board that is 0 hard with every pair matched. Measured on a copy before it was turned on: 1 locked via removed of 621 on 38 zones, 0 left alone, hard 0 and unrouted 3 both unchanged, so nothing opened. It stays judged against the board before it (finish.sh 5b) and reverts if it opens anything.
finish._direct_close_why: 12 September 2026, A24. After the stub router had closed 9 of 10 and then 2 of 3, three connections were left and the stub router refused all three. direct_close proposed each as geometry and the DRC judged it: /CELL+ closed as a straight 9.59 mm locked track (hard 0, opens 3 to 2), and the other two were refused with what they hit named, which is the half that matters as much: /+3V3 crosses /PI_KILL and /PI_SHDN_REQ on F.Cu and meets /HEAT_EN and /EMCON_HW on both inner layers, /VBUS20 bridges the solder mask of U3 pad 2 in all five shapes. Declared for A alone: C10's eleven opens are 39 to 298 mm and this tool declines every one of them, which is the correct answer and not a reason to run it there. BUDGET, 16 September 2026: 5,400 seconds. 16 September 2026. The re-finish of A35 spent all 1,800 seconds on FIVE of thirteen open pairs and stopped in the middle of a shape, reporting 'the budget ran out' for the eight it never reached. Each candidate costs a design-rule check and this board's DRC is seven seconds (240 by 160 mm, six layers, 5,000 tracks), so thirteen pairs at roughly ten shapes each is an hour of DRC before anything else. Ninety minutes is that with room; it is wall time on a box that is at four percent of its cores, and the alternative is a stage that reports a budget rather than an answer. It lives INSIDE this block because finish.sh's cfg strips a `direct_close_` prefix and looks in here: declared at the finish level it was read as a key of a block that does not have it, and the stage spent 1,809 seconds of an 1,800 second default while the declaration said 5,400. Same shape as the 12 September pruner that was declared at the top level where cfg could not see it.
finish._stub_env_why: 12 September 2026, A24, measured on a copy before it was declared. With the 0.1 mm grid and a 2.5-fold window the stub router closed 9 of 10 opens and then 0 of the last 2; with a 0.05 mm grid, a six-fold window and an 80 M node cap it closed BOTH of those two (/+3V3 with a single via, /VBUS20 with 11 tracks and a via), hard 0 throughout. The finer grid is what lets it see between the pads of U3, where /VBUS20's approach has to pass. It costs time, which is why `stub_timeout_s` exists: a cut run leaves the board as it was.
finish._rail_prune_why: 15 September 2026, A32: 0 hard, 0 unrouted, and four rails MISSED where the rail copper alone reads MET, because the router laid its own 0.5 mm inner tracks in parallel with the bands it cannot see (VIN_RAW: a 0.5 mm In2 track the whole west side beside the 6 mm B.Cu band, carrying 0.63 A at ratio 1.60). A router piece on a rail net comes off when the net stays connected without it.
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.

widen.why: the case this tool was written for: the router laid this rail at its class width 0.4 mm for 63.9 mm on B.Cu at 1.0 A, 134 mV, 2.68 percent of 5 V against the 1.5 percent this board declares as its share of the rail's end-to-end budget

16 September 2026, the solved board: a 0.500 mm conductor on In2.Cu at (58.0, 158.5) carries 1.46 A against 0.40 A for its own cross-section at 10 K, ratio 3.69, which is this rail's worst item and the board's
the same reading: 0.500 mm on In2.Cu at (59.9, 151.4), 8.8 mm long, 0.63 A against 0.40 A
the same reading: 0.500 mm on In2.Cu at (68.1, 81.2), 13.3 mm long, 0.66 A against 0.40 A

finish._widen_why: 16 September 2026. These are conductors the ROUTER laid, on a rail whose own copper is drawn by power_copper.py, and they carry real current in the solved mesh rather than being the parallel decoration rail_prune takes off. Widening the tracks that are already there changes no topology: same path, same vias, same pads, more copper, kept only if the hard and unrouted counts do not rise. The inner layers are 0.5 oz, which is why 0.5 mm carries 0.40 A there and 1.23 A on an outer layer.
finish._via_parallel_why: 18 September 2026 (rule PI-003): after every copper-editing stage and before the ground vias, via_parallel lays parallel barrels beside any via dc_drop's solved mesh puts over IPC-2221's rating for its wall (the fabricator's 18 um plating), joined on every layer the net touches there, DRC-guarded, then re-solves and re-judges. On the committed board: A32 fails five rails (VBUS20 3.40 A through a 0.90 A barrel)

_pair_order_why: 12 September 2026: A's three ribbon pairs sit on J_AB1, two of them on the header's end rows and USB_WALL on an inner row, which can only leave through the 1.14 mm channel between the columns. Laid longest-first the end-row pairs go down and their copper crosses USB_WALL's fan out of the connector, and the pass ends 2 of 3; laid with USB_WALL first it is 3 of 3. The pass is greedy and never rips up, so the pair with the least freedom goes first.
_phase_why: 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh set it for one board of six. A board's silk then names a phase `verify_deliverable` refuses, after the route, which is how A24 came to carry A18 on its front silk. `full.sh` exports this unless the caller has already set PHASE. 16 September 2026 00:15 CEST: A35 -> A36 (the route in flight is the one the set cuts; final_gate refuses a folder that is not the declared phase). 17 SEPTEMBER 2026, THE DECLARATION IS THE BOARD IN THIS TREE AND NOT THE ROUTE IN FLIGHT. It was set to the in-flight phase on 16 September with the reason that final_gate refuses a folder that is not the declared one, and that is exactly what went wrong: every reader that GATES on this field asks 'is this folder the board', so pointing it at a route that has not landed makes those gates answer about a board that does not exist. Board P proved the cost: its P4 folder holds the board this tree holds, byte for byte (sha256 d79865e7b1aceb95), and it was being read as stale against a declared P5 that was measured, refused and abandoned under decision 28. Board A declared A36, a route that was never cut, while the tree carries A32. The phase in flight belongs to the RUN (`routeflow --phase`, with ROUTEFLOW_PHASE_UNDECLARED=1 for an arm whose board may never be adopted), and it moves into this field in the same commit that brings the board in.
region_overflow_allow_mm_reason: A24 reads 0 hard on the placed board with NODE 1.0 mm and FES 1.4 mm outside their rectangles: both spill into free board, measured 12 September 2026. The number is the measurement plus a tenth, not a default, and it drops to zero when those two regions are sized.
_pair_env_why: 14 September 2026, measured on A's own placed board, one variable. At the tool's default corridor slack the pre-router lays 3 of 3 pairs and leaves USB_D8's two legs 1.78 mm apart, which the owner's 1 mm length gate refuses and no meander can fix: every bump the leg-length matcher proposes is refused by the leg's own map, because A's pair corridors have no free copper beside them. At 0.30 (slim 0.10) the same board lays the same 3 of 3 and **USB_D8 comes out inside the matcher's own half-millimetre tolerance**, so it never needs a bump: a wider corridor is a straighter path, and a straighter path is two legs of the same length. USB_WALL stays 1.47 mm apart at both values and is owner decision 25.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

_gnd_grid_why: MEASURED ON THIS BOARD, 17 September 2026, and NOT declared. A41 declares gnd_grid 2.1 mm and A40 does not; same tree, same tools, same board, same router invocation and the same five hour cap. The grid lays 4,000 locked ground vias (the routed board carries 4,650 vias against A40's 902). Rule RET-004, each board judged at its own stem beside its own intent so the classification is the rule's: A41 reads 33 signal vias without a ground via within 1.5 mm of 52 judged, A40 reads 46 of 58. So the grid answers thirteen of them and leaves thirty-three; it does not close the rule. It costs this board nothing in copper terms that showed: 23 open connections against 25 at the cap, and pour_stitch found 0 islands to repair against 4. That is the opposite of board C, where the grid cost 21 open connections, and of board P, where it cost the route. WHY IT IS STILL NOT DECLARED: the board this tree holds is A32, which is 0 hard and 0 unrouted and reads 32 lacking of 40 judged, while BOTH arms are open boards that their own finishes refused. A grid that does not close the rule is a change to make when the rule's criterion is ruled (owner decisions 32 and 39), not before, and 4,000 extra drilled vias on a six-layer board is a fabrication cost to put to the owner with that ruling rather than to take quietly.
_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): six layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
_stitch_cap_mm_why: Rule RET-003, 16 September 2026. Board A's In2 carries a GND pour and a VBAT pour side by side, and 35 of its signal vias change reference between the two: measured with ref_change.py, which samples the fill in a ring around each via because the fill retreats from the via's own barrel. A return current that has to cross between two different reference conductors crosses at a capacitor or it goes the long way round, so the question is how far that capacitor may sit. THREE MILLIMETRES IS OURS, not a source: it is the same distance this project already declares for a decoupling capacitor from the pin it serves, and using one number for the same physics is better than using two. The rule stays GENERATED_ONLY until a document states it.
_via_ring_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, the VIA rows rather than the annular ring row. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): minimum via diameter 0.25 mm on a minimum via hole of 0.15 mm for 2 or more layers, which leaves 0.05 mm of copper per side. The PTH annular ring row (0.20 mm) is stated for a plated COMPONENT hole and cannot bind a via, because no via at this document's own minimum could satisfy it; board D12 was refused on 16 September for a 0.45/0.20 via at 0.125 mm of ring, which is what that confusion costs.
_copper_layers_why: Six layers since 7 September 2026. Under the P0 ruling of 11 September this is OPEN: the record's own note says A's 33 hard on four layers turned out to be one router knot, and no four-layer rerun with unknot.py was ever done. The number lives here so that answering P0 is a declaration and not an edit to a gate.

external_ports.why: shore and vehicle DC arriving over the dock from the wall receptacle; the USB pair and the spare on this same connector are board A to board E INSIDE the case and are not external conductors
the wall USB host port through the MIL-DTL-38999 receptacle: a person plugs a stranger's stick into this
the USB-C outlet on the connector plate, out of the case

_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. A port that leaves the ENCLOSURE is a wire a person will plug something into, in the rain, having walked across a floor. Every one of them reaches a semiconductor, and the only thing between is a suppressor, a choke, a series resistor into a clamp, or nothing. Most connectors on these boards are internal (board-to-board ribbons, module sockets, fan leads inside a sealed case) and treating every J as external would refuse every board for wires that never leave it. The board knows which is which and nothing else does, so each one is named with where it goes.

GND.what: the board's single ground: every return on this board is this net

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k

logo.why: 16 September 2026: silk_space.py reports an 80 by 31 mm rectangle free of every footprint at case (49.9, 27.5) on this board, which is the sticker master's own size. 60 mm is taken instead of 80 so the mark keeps 10 mm of clear silk on each side, and the centre is the 60 mm candidate's own

prelay_groups.why: 16 September 2026, rule RF-001: all eleven of these ten-millimetre blind-mate paths were routed on In2.Cu at the RF class's 0.350 mm, which computes 25.5 ohm on this stackup against the 50 the class itself declares. The width is right for an OUTER layer, where the same copper is about 50, so the remedy is the layer and not the width: they are laid outside before the router runs, where there is room, and rf_line.py reads the result back off the routed board.

_prelay_nets_why: MEASURED AND REFUSED, 17 September 2026. A40 pre-lays /CH_ACN, /CH_SRP, /FE_LDRV1 and /PD_EN on all four copper layers before the router sees the board; A42 is A40 with that stage removed and nothing else changed (its chain log carries guard-prelay-group and no guard-prelay). Both ran to the same five hour cap with the same invocation: A40 ended at 25 open of 254 nets having managed 55 passes at 3.3 minutes each, A42 at 15 open having managed about 137 at 2.2 minutes each. So pre-laid copper costs this board ten connections and half again the time per pass, which is the router having to route around copper it did not choose. The eleven RF nets of prelay_groups STAY: rule RF-001 requires them on an outer layer and that is a requirement rather than a knob.
_sense_clearance_why: WHY THE TWO SENSE LINES RUN TOO CLOSE, and what the fix has to reckon with (17 September 2026, rule ANA-001). POE_CS runs 0.182 mm from POE_SW2 over 10.79 mm and B33_FB 0.350 mm from B33_SW over 8.47 mm, both outside the shared part's courtyard, and the declaration asks 0.50 mm. THE ROUTER DID WHAT THE CLASSES TOLD IT: POE_CS is in class SW at 0.127 mm of clearance and POE_SW2 in HV at 0.18, so 0.18 is the bar it honoured, and B33_FB is in no pattern at all and falls to Default. The obvious fix is a SENSE class at the 0.50 mm the declaration asks for, which the router would honour because a class reaches the DSN; what it has to reckon with is that a class clearance has no courtyard exemption, so 0.50 mm would also apply where the sense line approaches the shunt's own pads, which is where it must go. Measure that geometry on the board before declaring the class: if the shunt's pad gap cannot hold 0.50, the class is the wrong instrument and the answer is placement. Freerouting reads DSN classes and not KiCad's custom rules, so a per-net-pair keep-away cannot be expressed any other way. MEASURED, AND THE CLASS IS REFUSED (17 September 2026, same hour). Pad edge to pad edge on A42's board, the nearest OTHER-NET pad to each conductor's own pads: POE_CS is 0.820 mm from the FETs' own switching pads at Q18 and Q19, 0.660 from their gate drives, 1.760 at the divider R72, and **0.250 mm at U16 pin 16**, the controller's own fine-pitch pin, whose neighbour is GND; B33_FB is 0.850 mm at both divider resistors and **0.200 mm at U12 pin 8**, whose neighbour is B33_SS. A 0.50 mm class has no courtyard exemption, so it would refuse the escape at those two pins and the route would die at the source rather than ten millimetres away. So the class is the wrong instrument at 0.50: what is left is a smaller class value that the pins can hold (0.25 is the floor those two pins set), or PLACEMENT, putting the sense network so its run stays inside the courtyard the rule already exempts, or a declared exemption per net with its reason. The placement is the one that answers the rule as written.

_safety_lines_why: Board A gates its own transmitters with EMCON_HW and can be switched off by PI_KILL, so those two are judged here; the other three cross this board between a ribbon and a connector and are judged where a part reads them. Every one of the five has its pull on this board, which is the property the rule asks for: a missing panel leaves the transmitters silent and the kit running.
_rf_line_why: ELEVEN RF PORTS AT 26 OHM, AND THE WIDTH IS NOT WHAT IS WRONG (17 September 2026, rule RF-001, which this board was outside of until its board list was corrected to match its own condition). Every one of board A's eleven RF nets runs EXACTLY 10.0 mm on In2.Cu at 0.35 mm, which the board's own stackup makes a 26 ohm stripline against the class's 50 ohm target, 49 percent low. The width is right: board D carries the same 0.35 mm RF class and passes RF-001 on twelve segments, because its runs are on an OUTER layer, where 0.35 mm is about 50 ohm. What board A has is a LAYER problem, and it comes from the geometry: J_RF<k> is the SMA jack on the top and J_BM<k> the SMP-MAX blind-mate receptacle on the UNDERSIDE, 10 mm south of it, so every port has to cross the board and the router took the whole crossing on one inner layer rather than a short run and a transition. The eleven lengths being identical to a tenth of a millimetre is what says it is systematic. THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, for the generation after A43: lay each port yourself, locked, as an outer-layer run from the jack to a point over the receptacle with a single via into its pad, which is the geometry board D already passes on; the cost has to be measured first, and this board's own arms say pre-laid copper is EXPENSIVE on it, the other way round from the first reading of this note: the routeflow journals have A40, which pre-lays four nets, at 25 unrouted of 254 and A42, which is A40 with those four removed and nothing else changed, at 15, so pre-laying cost this board ten connections and half again the time per pass. A43 routes without them. What is different about the eleven RF drops is that each is 10 mm in the south edge between two FIXED parts rather than a crossing of the board, and that they are already laid, by the router, on the wrong layer: the choice is not whether that copper exists but who chooses its layer. Nothing was changed while A43 routes. CORRECTED AND ANSWERED THE SAME EVENING (appendix 32.221): the width IS part of what is wrong, because board D passes at 0.35 mm on an outer layer for its 7628 four-layer stack's 0.2 mm of prepreg under F.Cu, and this six-layer 3313 stack puts 0.0994 mm (er 4.1) there: rf_line's own microstrip form with its 0.967 correction reads 0.35 mm on this board's F.Cu as 22.8 ohm, 0.15 as 48.2 and 0.14 as 50.1. gen_pcb_a3.py lays the eleven drops itself now, locked on F.Cu from the SMA centre pin to the blind-mate centre pin, straight and clear of every other net's copper on the placement, and the RF class is 0.14 mm; the first regeneration at 0.35 mm read all eleven at 23.5 ohm and the board's placed gate, escapes and hard set were unchanged (0 hard). The route has eleven connections fewer to make, the opposite of the pre-lay that cost it ten: these are ten millimetres between two fixed parts at the south edge, laid where the router had already laid them on the wrong layer.
_thermal_pads_why: 17 September 2026, thermal_pads.py on the cut A32: 39 exposed pads, 32 with no via of their own net inside them. The 25 PowerPAK SO-8 drain pads (the converters' switching FETs, 14.90 mm2 each, nearest same-net via 2.2 to 14.1 mm) are carried by the top-side rail islands and bands by design (32.39) and get no via; the seven SOIC-8 exposed-pad parts (the three TPS2596 eFuses U21 to U23 and U4 to U7 on the same land, 6.87 mm2, GND) have no via and the nearest ground via is 4.31 to 5.09 mm away while In1, In2 and In4 ground copper is directly underneath. escape.py lays thermal vias in FINE-PITCH parts only, so no stage ever asked. The seven HTSSOP and QFN parts carry five each. ANSWERED IN escape.py the same evening: the exposed-pad block ran only inside the fine-pitch loop and runs for every footprint now; on a copy of A32's placed board it laid 103 thermal vias in the 31 coarse tabs, 0 refused for the other side, hard 0 before and after, and every one of the 39 exposed pads carries a via of its net. The next A generation carries them by construction.
_ana_001_arm_why: THE INSTRUMENT ANA-001 HAS BEEN MISSING, named 17 September 2026 23:25 CEST (not yet written): a per-net-pair keep-away cannot reach Freerouting through KiCad's custom rules, and a class clearance at the declared 0.50 mm cannot escape the sense pins (POE_CS 0.250 mm at U16 pin 16, B33_FB 0.200 at U12 pin 8), but the DSN's own structure section carries CLASS-PAIR clearances, (class_class (classes SENSE SW) (rule (clearance 0.5))), which apply between two nets of different classes and NOT inside a class, so a SENSE class for the declared sensitive nets with a 0.50 mm class-pair rule against SW and HV leaves each net's own escape at its class clearance and holds it 0.50 mm from a switching net everywhere else. fr_rules.py writes the rules block and dsn_export.sh the DSN, and neither emits class_class today. The arm: A43's board first (does it repeat POE_CS 10.79 mm and B33_FB 8.47 mm), then one route with the class-pair rule against A43, one variable.
_a44_a45_why: Two arms launched 17 September 2026 21:30 UTC on the hub against A43 (250 passes, 10 h route cap, same placement recipe from the runner's phase directory with today's tools): A44 = A43's configuration + the eleven RF drops laid by the generator on F.Cu at 0.14 mm (32.221) + the SENSE class for the nineteen declared sensitive nets (default geometry, so POE_CS goes 0.5 to 0.25 mm wide); A45 = A44 + FR_CLASS_CLEAR=SENSE:SW:0.5,SENSE:HV:0.5, the class-pair clearance in the DSN (32.222), and nothing else. Read A43, A44 and A45 side by side when they land: unrouted after the router and after the closers, RF-001, ANA-001's two runs (POE_CS 10.79 mm, B33_FB 8.47 mm on A32), and the pass cost. _cs_filter_why: 18 September 2026 12:50 CEST (rule ANA-001, lm5176-datasheet.pdf clause 9.1 and section 8.2.2.7). Board A's five LM5176 stages tied pin 15 (CSG) to the GROUND NET and carried no filter on the current-sense pair. TI's own pin table says of pin 15: 'Connect directly to the low-side (ground) of the current sense resistor', and its layout clause says 'Use Kelvin connections to RSENSE for the current sense signals CS and CSG and run lines in parallel from the RSENSE terminals to the IC pins. Avoid crossing noisy areas such as SW1 and SW2 nodes ... Place the filter capacitor for the current sense signal as close to the IC pins as possible'. With CSG on the plane, every millivolt of plane drop between the shunt's ground pad and wherever the router joined that pin adds to a sensed voltage whose own limit threshold is 120 to 140 mV (VCS(BUCK)). The generator now lays 100 R in each line with 1 nF across the pins (8.2.2.7: 'The filter resistance should not exceed 100 Ohm'), which costs the offset current alone (IOFFSET 19 uA x 100 R = 1.9 mV, 1.4 percent of the threshold) because the bias current is common to both lines. Fifteen parts: R150/R151/C123 (FE), R152/R153/C124 (PA), R154/R155/C125 (HF), R156/R157/C126 (POE), R158/R159/C127 (PD); each capacitor is declared as its controller's pin 16 decoupling so bypass_slots seats it at the pin and DEC-001 measures it. Proved on the hub at PHASE=A47: 421 footprints against 406, erc_gate PASS, region fit 3 overflowing of 25 at 1.4 mm against the declared 1.5 allowance (PAQ grew 3.0 mm east and HFQ 4.0 mm south, which is all the room region_room measures there), check_pcb_a ALL PASS, and FE_CSF reads C123.1 + R150.2 + U2.16 with FE_CSGF C123.2 + R151.2 + U2.15. THE READING THIS COSTS, said in advance: board A's committed board is A32, cut before the filter existed, so ANA-001 on it reads 15 failures of 24 declared and TEN of them are 'declared sensitive and the board has no such net' (the five stages' CSF and CSGF). That is the same shape as the four CH_*_F charger nets on 17 September and it is right: a declaration that names nothing stays a failure, and the cause is the board being five phases behind its generators. The four charger nets and the five FB dividers are the real measurements on A32; the ten go when an A4x board that carries the filter is adopted.
_cs_shunt_placement_why: MEASURED ON A32 the same hour, and NOT yet answered: each stage's CS shunt sits 5.9 to 17.6 mm from its nearest low-side FET and up to 43.8 mm from the farthest (FE R12 14.1, PA R56 5.9, HF R122 5.9, POE R72 17.6, PD R127 17.6), and that node is the four FETs' common source, so the full switched current runs those millimetres before it reaches the element that senses it. The datasheet asks for the RSENSE ground pin as close as possible to CIN and COUT. The next A placement pass gives the five shunts and their two filter resistors FIXED seats at their stage's low-side FETs, the way the rails' islands and bands are placed; the region lists alone do not decide adjacency. Board A's FE stage is the odd one: its shunt and its ISNS resistor sit in the SUPPORT region FES while the other four stages keep both with the FETs.
_a47_route_why: A47 (18 September 2026 11:11 UTC, /root/arf47, $SP/a47.sh): board A's next phase and the first that carries the LM5176 current-sense filter and the Kelvin CSG (fifteen parts), beside everything A44 carried: the RF drops at 0.14 mm, the SENSE class, thermal vias in every exposed pad and the one class table. 250 passes and a ten-hour cap, the ceiling A43 to A45 were given. It is a REGENERATION, so its placement is new and its open count is not comparable pass for pass with the A4x arms; what it answers is the instruments.
